### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/declarative-endpoints.mdx`  _(via record_change (literal, a string literal in runStackExpressionPasses))_
- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via record_change (literal, a string literal in runStackExpressionPasses))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via record_change (literal, a string literal in runStackExpressionPasses))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via record_change (literal, a string literal in runStackExpressionPasses))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `current_user (literal, 42 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2bc3a1a737633cde5e15b1bdd560b2b5dacd8302` — the merge of head `c7417c1fc82d413709beb46dda9d1a175e650fc4` into base `6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2bc3a1a737633cde5e15b1bdd560b2b5dacd8302 && git checkout 2bc3a1a737633cde5e15b1bdd560b2b5dacd8302
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765 c7417c1fc82d413709beb46dda9d1a175e650fc4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765 && git merge --no-ff c7417c1fc82d413709beb46dda9d1a175e650fc4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c7417c1fc82d413709beb46dda9d1a175e650fc4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts + .changeset/29026-flow-condition-null-guard.md (read for ②), packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/flow-cel-root-scope.ts, packages/lint/src/flow-variable-scope.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/test/notify-recipient-optional-fields.test.ts, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md

Inputs read: card #29026 body and all four comments (triage 6572724715, claim 6579715842, os-dev-report 6581777047, claim amendment 6581859809); PR #29474 body, file list (6 paths) and the net diff against base 8ca9dd7b (632 insertions, 121 deletions, matches the API diff); the check-runs on the head at writing time: 60 runs, 22 success, 9 skipped, 29 still in progress — Test UI (16 shards), Test Core (8 shards), Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. Concluded success includes Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, every Lint lane, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate (its three shards and Dogfood Verify CLI skipped by path), Flag docs affected by code changes. None failed. The record is written before the in-progress runs conclude; the adopting seat confirms every check green before the queue, as the Tier S rule requires.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept-set change, the narrowing itself: a flow whose `resolveFlowTriggerKind` is `record_change` with a declared start `objectName` now has its start `config.condition`, every edge `condition` (container regions included) and every `decision` `conditions[].expression` judged by `findUnguardedNullableOperands`, severity `error`, outcome `run-fails`. RIGHT. Read against the engine on main: `evaluateCondition` (dag-traversal.ts) throws on a non-ok CEL result (ADR-0032 §1c, never a quiet false); `execute()` records a loud flow failure; the record-change trigger handler catches and swallows so the write lands (record-change-trigger.ts, the error-isolation catch). `buildContext` runs both `record` and `previous` through `materializeDeclaredFields` whenever the prior row is in hand or the event is an insert, so the binding is total and `!= null` is the sound prescription, exactly as on validation rules and hook conditions. The message's outcome clause ("the flow run fails at this condition: the write that fired it still lands") matches the code.
2. Accept-set change, bare names: a bare identifier is judged as `record.name` only when `flowCelRootScope(...).provable` holds, the name is a nullable field of the trigger object, and it is neither in `collectFlowVariableNames` (declared variables, inputs, outputVariable, iterator, error variables, screen fields, assignment targets, node ids) nor in `record` / `previous` / `vars` / `current_user`. RIGHT and conservative: `seedRunVariables` seeds declared variables first, binds `record`, then flattens the record's fields only where no variable holds the name, then binds `previous`; `celScope` layers `vars` / `current_user` over. A guard on either spelling guards both (both resolve to the key `record.name`), which is how the run reads them. One safe-direction blind spot noted, not a finding: a declared variable with no default and not supplied as input is never seeded, so the bare field IS flattened into that name at run time while the gate leaves it unjudged — a missed refusal, never a false one, and the #14089 shadow warning already covers that shape.
3. Accept-set change, start-condition presumption: `provenNonNullKeys(startCondition)` is presumed at every edge and branch. RIGHT: `execute()` evaluates the start condition before any node on every entrance (engine.ts, the trigger-condition gate); `executeWithoutRetry` does not re-evaluate it but is entered only after that gate passed on the same variable map. `truthGuards` unions over `&&`, intersects over `||` and `?:`, so a one-armed `||` proves nothing (pinned).
4. Accept-set change, macro and `cel.bind` scoping: a comprehension-bound or `cel.bind`-bound name is not the field inside its body; the receiver and the initialiser stay outside. RIGHT (mirrors `COMPREHENSION_MACROS` in flow-cel-root-scope.ts).
5. Accept-set WIDENING on every surface the gate covers (validation rules, hook conditions, `requiredWhen`, and the new flow slots): a `summary` field with `summaryOperations.function` `count` or `sum` is no longer nullable. Judged right against objectql on main: `summaryEmptySetValue` is 0 for count / sum, `initializeSummaryFields` seeds it on insert before `beforeInsert` hooks, `aggregateSummaryValue` falls back to it on an empty aggregate, and `summaryNullIsBackfillable` declares a stored NULL on those functions a hole. `min` / `max` / `avg` stay nullable. Measured on the showcase: `showcase_committee_quorum` (`total_amount` at-least 5000, a `sum`) is now not flagged, and the cited pin exists (`notify-recipient-optional-fields.test.ts` line 370 expects `total_amount` 0). One precision gap carried to ④ (should-fix 2): the always-valued claim presumes the one-off #6063 backfill ran on pre-#6013 parents.
6. Surfaces left out, each named right: a non-start node's `config.condition` (inert; `flow-inert-node-condition` reports it), flows with no record trigger (api body, action record, map item — nothing materializes them), a screen field's `visibleWhen` (different fault outcome, unmeasured), time-relative sweeps (not `record_change`; swept rows not shown to be materialized — conservative). At the runtime publish gate `perWriteSnapshotEntrance` opens the scope, so bare names are never judged there and `record.` / `previous.` reads are.
7. Public surface of `@objectstack/lint` (index.ts): the exported type `NullGuardOptions` gains two optional keys, `bareFields` and `presumed` — additive, every existing caller unchanged. `provenNonNullKeys` and the widened `NullGuardOutcome` (`run-fails`) are module exports not re-exported from the package index, so not public. `NullGuardFinding` is unchanged (the resolver's `key` stays internal). RIGHT for a `minor`.
8. Tests re-judged in place: the old "leaves flow conditions alone" case becomes the covered verdict with the inert-node and untriggered controls kept; three suites make `crm_lead.rating` required so their shape verdicts stay pinned; the keys-read meta-test declares `summaryOperations` on `def`, a `summaryOperations.function` receiver, and three plumbing receivers. Each is the minimal edit that keeps the pinned assertion meaningful. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29026-flow-condition-null-guard.md`: `@objectstack/lint: minor`. The diff moves one published package, `@objectstack/lint`, and nothing else. PR body and changeset both carry, line-initial, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. Per the level axis in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: a declared kind takes at least `minor` on a moved package — satisfied; `narrowed` beside a line carrying the `(narrowing)` arm — satisfied (the arm was added at c7417c1 after the claim amendment 6581859809; the earlier commits lacked it and would have been the contradiction). The kind is right: a flow an author could publish on main is refused on this head, and the count / sum widening is a second kind that `narrowed` outranks. A `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING: the changeset carries the FROM → TO fix (`budget != null &&` in front of the comparison, or the guard in the start condition) and the ADR-0087 disposition marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the gate lists; no authorable key is removed, so no tombstone is owed. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` concluded success on the head. Level judged right.

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report. None to answer.
- Deviation 1 (file surface widened to `validate-expressions.ts` and the new wiring test): answered by the claim amendment 6581859809; the file list matches the amended claim exactly.
- Deviation 2 (the claimed `showcase_committee_quorum` fixture fix not made): answered by measurement read in the tree — `total_amount` is a `sum` roll-up (flows/index.ts line 1937; the test pin at line 370), so the judge was fixed instead of the example. Right call under rule 12 (fix the producer of the false verdict, not the metadata).
- Deviation 3 (origin/main f95d0dba merged in): fine; the diff against base is clean.
- Out-of-scope class c (skills and docs say the gate rejects validation-rule or hook predicates only): the report says "noted, not filed", but the PR body names follow-up #29482, which exists and is open ("Teach the record-triggered flow null-guard gate in the formula skill and the flows page"). Answered. `skills/**` is governed and is correctly untouched here.
- Out-of-scope class b (`previous.x` on a create leg): noted, not filed. Escalated as should-fix 3 below — it is a metadata-authoring trap in the gate's own prescription, which rule 10 files rather than notes.
- `dogfood_battery: n/a — no ! in the PR title and no (narrowing) arm`: stale at this head. The arm was declared at c7417c1, after the report, and os-dev.md says the full battery runs once on the final head when the `Clause-②:` line carries `(narrowing)`. Escalated as should-fix 4; not a FAIL because the CI Dogfood Regression Gate concluded success on the head (shards path-skipped) and the dev measured the battery's catch class directly: the real judge over app-showcase (32 flows), app-crm (1) and app-todo (4) reports 0 null-guard findings, with the #28951 spelling as a positive control reporting exactly 1.
- PR body Verification cites head b4043790; the head is c7417c1, a changeset-only delta (the `(narrowing)` arm). Noted; the check-runs on c7417c1 are the verdict.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against the published spec on main. `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` teaches that conditions are strict CEL, that `has()` is not the escape hatch it looks, and that an absent or null operand aborts the run; `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` teaches `!= null` guards and `previous != null &&` on insert legs. The spec declares no capability that an unguarded ordering on a nullable field in a flow condition works — it declares the opposite, and the engine delivers the opposite (`evaluateCondition` throws). So this PR makes the spec's own refusal real at publish time; it takes no declared capability away at the consumer, and nothing is narrowed in a consumer in place of a producer fix (rule 12: reject at authoring). The remedy text is the one the spec teaches, and the ledger's `has()` measurement matches `materializeDeclaredFields`. The ledger row, the removed stale block in `validate-expressions.ts` and the gate are one change, read as one; the ledger's `binding` column still states facts about the surface, not verdicts, as the `readonlyWhen` row needs.

Attempts to break it, and their outcome:

- Retry path skipping the start gate: `executeWithoutRetry` does not re-evaluate the start condition, but is reached only from `execute()` after the gate held on the same seeded map. Holds.
- Delete events: `buildContext` builds the record from the prior row and materializes it when the prior row is in hand. Holds.
- A record-triggered flow also launched by an action handing an empty record: the ledger says this explicitly and names the guard safe on both bindings (`has(record.x) && record.x != null`), which `truthGuards` on `&&` accepts. Holds, by declared choice.
- A `script` / `connector_action` / `wait` / `subflow` / `map` node, or a contract-less screen: the bound set is unprovable, bare names unjudged, `record.` still judged (pinned). Holds.
- Pre-#6013 parents: see should-fix 2.
- The two doors disagreeing: see should-fix 1.

Findings:

- should-fix 1 — Build and runtime publish doors can disagree in the runtime-stricter direction. At `os validate` a start condition `budget != null` (bare) proves `record.budget` and an edge comparing `record.budget` with an ordering operator passes; at the runtime publish gate the bare set is empty (`perWriteSnapshotEntrance` opens the scope), the presumption is not derived, and the same edge is refused. Mixed spelling is unusual, and deriving the presumption from a bare guard with an unprovable bound set would be unsound, so the choice is defensible; but a flow that `os validate` accepts and the publish gate refuses is a trap the ledger does not record. Record it in the ledger's flow row and the changeset's "At the runtime publish gate" sentence, or make the runtime gate stand down on the presumption-dependent finding the way the entrance judgment stands down.
- should-fix 2 — `isAlwaysValuedSummary`'s doc comment says the engine "backfills a stored NULL with it", which reads as automatic. On main the backfill is the one-off `os migrate summary-nulls` (`summary-backfill.ts`, #6063); `initializeSummaryFields` is create-time only and "existing rows are untouched". A pre-#6013 parent never backfilled still reads NULL, and on a validation rule that fault is fail-closed on the write. The widening is sound under the engine's contract (a NULL count / sum is declared a hole), but the comment and the changeset bullet "Fewer findings elsewhere" should say the judgment presumes the migration ran.
- should-fix 3 — `previous.x` on a create leg. The gate reports an unguarded `previous.x` and prescribes `!= null`; on a `record-after-write` / insert flow `previous` is bound to `null` (`seedRunVariables`), so `previous.x != null` itself faults and the full guard is `previous != null && previous.x != null`. The prescription is incomplete, not wrong (the unguarded read faulted there too), but the dev's own classification is a metadata-authoring trap, which rule 10 files as a card rather than notes. File it; the hint could name `previous != null &&` for a `previous.` operand.
- should-fix 4 — The `dogfood_battery` line is stale on the final head: the `(narrowing)` arm makes the battery owed under os-dev.md. Run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` on c7417c1 and amend the report, or have the adopting seat record that the example-app probe (0 findings; positive control 1) plus the green CI Dogfood Regression Gate stand as the measurement.

No must-fix found. The narrowing is the right direction, is delivered by the code it cites, and its refusals are real at the engine.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:devx#1` · head `c7417c1fc82d413709beb46dda9d1a175e650fc4` · 2026-11-02T16:39Z

1. **Shape:** six files: `packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.ts`, `validate-expressions.ts`, their tests, the new `validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts`, and `.changeset/29026-flow-condition-null-guard.md` (minor, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, ADR-0087 marker). Inside the claim as amended (6581859809: the wiring lives in `validate-expressions.ts`; no example-app edit, `showcase_committee_quorum` measured a false positive and answered by the `count` / `sum` roll-up rule).
2. **Premise, measured:** the ledger row "flow / edge `condition`" on `main` was excluded only by the "widening tracked separately (#4811)" clause; the run reads every declared field (`materializeDeclaredFields`) and `evaluateCondition` throws on the CEL fault while the record-change trigger swallows it so the write lands. Read off the code by the contract reviewer (record 6582253324 ①) and by the dev (report 6581777047). Positive control: the #28951 spelling gives 1 finding on the branch, 0 on `main`.
3. **Gates:** local 58 derived / 58 run / all exit 0; `@objectstack/lint` full suite 190/190 files, 7852/7852 tests (report). CI on this head: 54 success, 9 expected skips, none red. The full dogfood battery (should-fix 4, follow-up report 6582613426) was red on 4 cases in `flow-runas.dogfood.test.ts` and `declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest.dogfood.test.ts`; the dev reproduced them with `packages/lint/src` reset to the merge base. The seat read them as the closed main-red #29426, fixed on `main` by #29451 (`6af3d295`), which is not in this branch's base (`f95d0dba`); the merge queue tests against a `main` that has it. Not this PR's.
4. **Accepted deviations:** the file-surface widening and the dropped example edit, both in claim amendment 6581859809. `Fixes` / `Clause-②` / `Metadata-protocol` / `Skills-docs` sit above `## 维护者速读` (os-dev order); the PR body's Verification cites `b4043790`, and `c7417c1f` differs from it by the changeset line only.
5. **Out of scope:** filed #29482 (`Skills-docs: follow-up #29482`: `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` and `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` teach the new flow slots) and #29491 (the contract review's should-fix 1–3: build vs runtime door divergence, the `isAlwaysValuedSummary` backfill wording, the `previous.x` create-leg hint). Both rung to triage (6581907284, 6582302613).
6. **Landing:** not governed (`packages/lint/**`), under 3000 changed lines. The narrowing owes a same-head contract-review-tier PASS: record 6582253324 on `c7417c1f` (Served-tier `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, Local-runs none), claim 6582019844. Seat lands it: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` now, every check on this head green or an expected skip.
